1. Overview
===========

Chronicles of Aethermoor is an open-world action-RPG in which the player
takes on the role of Kira, a disgraced knight who must reclaim her honour
by saving the kingdom from an ancient magical curse.

The game targets PC and current-generation consoles.  The expected play
session length is 40–60 hours for the main story.

GAME OVERVIEW
=============

Genre: Action-RPG
Target Platform: PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X
Target Audience: Fans of open-world RPGs aged 16+
Core Loop: Explore → Combat → Loot → Upgrade → Explore

2. Core Mechanics
=================

2.1 Combat System
-----------------

The player engages enemies using a real-time, action-based combat system.
Controls are responsive and allow for fluid combos.

The player character has the following combat abilities:
- Light Attack: fast, low-damage strike.
- Heavy Attack: slow, high-damage strike with a brief charge animation.
- Dodge: iframe-based evasion in any direction.
- Block: parries incoming attacks if timed correctly, staggering the enemy.

Enemy AI will adapt to the player's playstyle over time. If the player
consistently uses heavy attacks, enemies will increase their guard frequency.

2.2 Progression System
-----------------------

Kira gains experience points (XP) by defeating enemies, completing quests,
and exploring new areas.  On level-up, the player receives skill points.

Skill points can be spent in three skill trees:
  1. Sword Mastery — increases melee damage and unlocks combo attacks.
  2. Arcane Arts — grants access to elemental spells and mana pool upgrades.
  3. Shadow Step — improves stealth and unlocks assassination skills.

3. World Design
===============

3.1 Hub World: The City of Aethermoor
---------------------------------------

Aethermoor serves as the primary hub. It contains:
- The Blacksmith: allows weapon upgrades and crafting.
- The Market: a dynamic economy where item prices fluctuate based on
  player supply and demand.
- The Tavern: quest board and NPC social interactions.
- The Royal Archives: lore repository and fast-travel unlock map.

Players can purchase property in Aethermoor to use as a personal base.

3.2 Regions
-----------

The world contains five explorable regions:
1. The Verdant Plains — starting area, low-difficulty enemies, tutorial quests.
2. The Ashwood Forest — mid-game area, stealth-focused encounters.
3. The Iron Wastes — high-difficulty area, stronghold sieges.
4. The Sunken Depths — underwater exploration with pressure-management mechanic.
5. The Aether Rift — endgame area, boss encounters, final story act.

4. User Interface
=================

4.1 HUD
-------

The HUD displays the following information:
- Health bar (top-left): Kira's current and maximum HP.
- Mana bar (top-left, below HP): current and maximum mana.
- Stamina bar (bottom-centre): depletes on dodge, sprint, and heavy attacks.
- Mini-map (top-right): shows nearby enemies, landmarks, and quest markers.
- Active quest tracker (right side): shows the current objective text.

4.2 Inventory Screen
--------------------

The inventory is a grid-based system.  Items are represented by icon tiles.
Equipment slots are shown on a character silhouette on the left panel.
The player can compare items by hovering over them.

5. Audio Design
===============

Music adapts dynamically to the game state using a layered soundtrack system.
Combat music triggers when an enemy enters the player's detection radius.
Ambient music fades in during exploration.

Sound effects are spatially positioned to support 3D audio environments.
